section_title: 6. RESPONSES TO HALT LAND DEGRADATION AND TO RESTORE DEGRADED LAND
summary: This document outlines various strategies for halting land degradation and restoring degraded land, including conservation agriculture, integrated crop-livestock-forestry systems, agroecology, agroforestry, and integrated watershed management. It also discusses responses to forest, rangeland, and urban land degradation.

heading_path: 6. RESPONSES TO HALT LAND DEGRADATION AND TO RESTORE DEGRADED LAND
passages.text: Conservation agriculture, as defined by the FAO, is characterized by three specific actions including: (i) continuous minimum mechanical soil disturbance; (ii) permanent organic soil cover; and (iii) diversification of crop species grown in sequences and/or associations.

heading_path: 6. RESPONSES TO HALT LAND DEGRADATION AND TO RESTORE DEGRADED LAND
Integrated crop, livestock and forestry systems
passages.text: Integrated crop and livestock has been used to restore degraded croplands in North America, Western Europe, Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina (Franzluebbers et al., 2014; Peyraud et al., 2014). Integrated crop and livestock - and integrated crop, livestock and forestry - have increased the amount of cultivated pasture in Brazil to nearly 101 million ha as compared to 57 million ha of native pasture.
passages.topic: Integrated crop, livestock and forestry systems

heading_path: 6. RESPONSES TO HALT LAND DEGRADATION AND TO RESTORE DEGRADED LAND
passages.text: They typically involve management practices such as cover crops, green manures, intercropping, agroforestry and crop-livestock mixtures that promote organic matter accumulation and nutrient cycling, soil biological activity, natural control mechanisms (disease suppression, biocontrol of insects, weed interference), resource conservation and regeneration (soil, water, germplasm), and general enhancements of agrobiodiversity and synergisms between components (Altieri, 2002; Gliessman, 2014).

heading_path: 6. RESPONSES TO HALT LAND DEGRADATION AND TO RESTORE DEGRADED LAND
passages.text: Agroforestry can reduce or reverse land degradation by: (i) maintaining soil fertility through increased carbon inputs, nitrogen fixation and nutrient cycling; (ii) reducing erosion; and (iii) conserving water (quantity and quality) through increased infiltration and reduced surface runoff.

heading_path: 6. RESPONSES TO HALT LAND DEGRADATION AND TO RESTORE DEGRADED LAND
passages.text: Therefore, combining improved plant genetics with decreased tillage and efficient use of fertilizer and irrigation water can not only increase soil organic carbon, but contribute to climate change mitigation (Lal, 2002).
